rulings.Case Title: RODNEY HAMPTON, JR. VS. LUKE O’BRIEN ET AL
rulings.Rulings: Set for Law and Motion/Discovery Calendar on Friday, August 07, 2026, Line 2. Defendants Luke O'Brien and Mel Murphy's demurrer to all five causes of action in the third amended complaint filed by plaintiff Rodney Hampton is a) overruled as to the first cause of action for breach of fiduciary duty, the second cause of action for fraudulent concealment, and the fifth cause of action for regulatory fraud/misuse of social equity program; and b) sustained without leave to amend as to the third cause of action for identity theft/fraud and deceit and the fourth cause of action for civil conspiracy. (The Court's complete tentative ruling has been emailed to the parties). For the 9:00 a.m. calendar, all attorneys and parties may appear in Department 302 remotely or in person. Remote hearings will be conducted by videoconference using Zoom. (Dept. 302 Zoom ID 160 409 7690; Passcode 516287.) To appear remotely at the hearing, go to the court's website at sfsuperiorcourt.org under "Online Services," navigate to "Tentative Rulings," and click on the appropriate link, or dial the corresponding phone number. Any party who contests a tentative ruling must send an email to contestdept302tr@sftc.org with a copy to all other parties by 4pm stating, without argument, the portion(s) of the tentative ruling that the party contests. The subject line of the email shall include the line number, case name and case number. The text of the email shall include the name and contact information, including email address, of the attorney or party who will appear at the hearing. Counsel for the prevailing party is required to prepare a proposed order which repeats verbatim the substantive portion of the tentative ruling and must email it to contestdept302tr@sftc.org prior to the hearing even if the tentative ruling is not contested. The court no longer provides a court reporter in the Law & Motion Department. Parties may retain their own reporter, who may appear in the courtroom or remotely. A retained reporter must be a California certified court reporter (CSR), for only a CSR's transcript may be used in California courts. If a CSR is being retained, include in your email all of the following: their name, CSR and telephone numbers, and their individual work email address. =(302/HEK)

rulings.Case Title: CASSIANA WRIGHT VS. BROOKE KIMBROUGH ET AL
rulings.Calendar Matter: Notice Of Motion And Motion To Compel Arbitration And Memorandum Of Points And Authorities In Support Thereof
rulings.Rulings: Set for Law and Motion/Discovery Calendar on Friday, August 07, 2026, Line 4. Defendant Brooke Kimbrough's motion to compel arbitration is granted. Per paragraph 11.13 of the Roots Operating Agreement, the parties must submit all six causes of action alleged by plaintiff Cassiana Wright to resolution by binding arbitration. The parties should meet and confer in an effort to identify an arbitrator or, failing that, a method for appointing an arbitrator. If the parties are unable to reach an agreement, one or both may file a petition provided for in the second paragraph of CCP 1281.6.
